I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over forty years. My father grew wheat and corn here, and so did his father. I know these fields — the soil is loamy, water comes from the deep well we share with two neighbors, and the county grain station still buys wheat at the support price. At my age, my back isn't what it was, so I rely on the machinery cooperative for ploughing and harvest. I'm not going to experiment with new crops I don't understand.

I have about 10 mu total. The obvious choice is the winter wheat / summer maize rotation — same land, two harvests per year. I'll plant 8 mu to wheat this autumn and follow it with maize on the same 8 mu next summer. The other 2 mu I keep as vegetable garden for the household — garlic, cabbage, that sort of thing. I won't include those in the plan below since it's just for eating.

For wheat I'll buy the improved Jimai-series seed from the township supply cooperative — same as last year. For maize I'll use Zhengdan 958 hybrid, which the seed dealer always has. I'll apply compound fertilizer at sowing and urea as topdress. Water is the worry — I'll irrigate at sowing, jointing, and heading for wheat. For maize the summer rains usually help, but I'll pump once if August is dry like last year.

I won't change my tillage. After maize harvest I rotary-till for wheat. For maize I direct-seed into the wheat stubble — saves time and diesel.
